competitive_landscape: Island transfers today are split between slow diesel catamarans (South Sea Cruises, Awesome Adventures) and expensive seaplane/helicopter. Neither is both fast and affordable; neither is clean. Foiling slots precisely into that gap — catamaran-like capacity at a fraction of the journey time, emission-free, across ideal protected reef water.

regulatory_note: Fiji's maritime sector is regulated by the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF); tourism transfers operate under established domestic frameworks. Tourism Fiji and the government promote sustainable tourism, supporting a zero-emission marine offering as both an environmental and brand fit.
seasonality: The Fijian dry season (May-October) is peak, with a warmer wetter cyclone-risk season November-April; the lee-side Mamanuca/Yasawa waters are largely protected, and resort demand sustains transfers year-round outside major weather events.

summary: Fiji is the South Pacific's tourism hub: nearly a million visitors a year arrive through Nadi and fan out to the Mamanuca and Yasawa island resorts, reached today by diesel catamaran (South Sea Cruises / Awesome Adventures) or seaplane and helicopter. Port Denarau is the gateway marina from which most island transfers depart. The Mamanucas sit just 10-20 nm offshore inside protected reef water, the Yasawas a little further — short, calm, sun-drenched legs that are ideal for Pioneer II, while ultra-luxury resorts (Laucala, Vomo, Likuliku, Kokomo) sustain a premium charter layer. With dense, established resort-transfer demand and only slow or expensive options today, Fiji is a natural fast-clean foiling island-shuttle market.
tagline: A million visitors a year funnel through Nadi to island resorts reached by slow catamaran. Protected reef water, dense resort demand — a foiling island-shuttle market waiting to happen.
